KidWatch is designed for caregivers who need clarity without exporting raw evidence everywhere.

KidWatch stores session evidence, screenshots, face crops, and viewer clusters only on the phone that captured them. The app may sync high-level usage summaries and content guidance to Firestore so family devices can compare daily trends, but it does not upload raw screenshots, raw face crops, or face-cluster thumbnails by default.

Use KidWatch only on phones you own or manage and only after informing the adults responsible for that device. When camera, usage access, Accessibility, or screenshot consent are granted, the app can observe foreground app sessions, create viewer clues, and capture screenshots for the apps you explicitly allow.

Local evidence is retained for %1$d days by default so working parents can review recent sessions without turning the phone into a permanent archive. You can delete evidence or wipe all local monitoring history at any time from Manage.
These product terms keep the app grounded in parental review, not covert surveillance.

KidWatch is intended for family-owned or family-managed phones used by children, parents, grandparents, and caregivers. You are responsible for obtaining any consent required in your household before enabling monitoring, screenshot capture, Accessibility capture, or viewer checks.

Do not rely on KidWatch as a guaranteed identity system. Viewer labels and clusters are helpful context, not legal proof of who used a device. Use the app to spot habits, repeated content patterns, and situations that need a family decision.

KidWatch may surface recommendations and AI-written summaries, but final parenting decisions remain with you. Review the underlying session details before acting on a recommendation, especially when limiting access, confronting a caregiver, or changing routines for a child.
Why screenshots and viewer clues stay local by default.

Screenshots, face crops, embeddings, and viewer clusters are sensitive family data. KidWatch keeps them on-device so the parent using that phone can review what happened without automatically copying raw evidence into cloud storage.

Only apps you mark for close review can generate Activity sessions, screenshots, or face capture. Usage access and Accessibility can stay on continuously once enabled. Automatic evidence can then keep viewer checks active in the background, while screenshots continue only as long as Android keeps the current screen-capture session alive. If camera, screenshot session, or Accessibility is missing, KidWatch continues with partial evidence instead of crashing.

You can remove all local evidence immediately from Manage. Clearing local monitoring history is broader: it also wipes app-usage history, session summaries, captured content activity, pending sync records, and content guidance stored on this phone.
